curtail

/kur-TAYL/ - rhymes with derail · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Curtail means to cut something back or cut it short, so that it goes on — but at a reduced level.

The park curtailed its evening hours after the storm damage, closing the gates at six instead of ten.

Example

Mid-drought, the vineyard curtailed irrigation by half: the vines still drank twice a week, but each row got minutes of water where it once had hours.

That is the shape of curtailing: the thing survives, smaller. The vines are still watered — just less. If the pumps had been shut off for good, curtail would be the wrong verb; the word always leaves a remainder.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

curb: to hold something back or keep it in check — restraint applied, while the thing may carry on much as before. Curtail actually cuts: after curtailing, there is measurably less of the thing than there was.

trim: to shave small amounts off the edges, often for neatness or thrift. Curtail is the deeper, harder cut, usually imposed from above — hours, budgets, and freedoms get curtailed, and everyone feels it.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

expand: to make something larger in scope or amount

prolong: to make something last longer

Where it sits · how much of the thing the cut removes

trim → curtail → abolish

trim vs. curtail: Trim is gentler than curtail: trimming shaves a little off the edges, while curtailing cuts a thing back sharply enough that everyone notices what is missing.

abolish vs. curtail: Abolish goes further than curtail: a curtailed service still runs, only less of it, while an abolished one is ended outright and wiped from the books.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — curt: cut short (Latin curtus)

Ending — -ail: respelled after English 'tail' — the word began as curtal, a horse with a docked tail

Put it together: Curt (cut short — Latin curtus) + -ail, an ending reshaped by the English word tail: a curtal was a cart-horse with its tail docked short, and to curtail was to dock. The image survives — whatever you curtail keeps moving, minus a visible length of itself.

Use the root in a new word: curt: Her reply was so curt that the new intern apologized twice for a question he had every right to ask.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / administrative

Curtail is the administrator's knife: schedules, budgets, services, rights, and liberties get curtailed — extents, not shapes. It promises two things at once: a real cut, and a remainder. Prune the roses and trim the hedge; curtail the watering schedule. And when nothing survives the decision at all, reach for abolish or scrap — curtail always leaves something running.
